title: Cascade Analytics - Time-to-First-Request PLG Discovery
summary: Initial PLG discovery focused on minimizing time-to-first-request for a developer self-serve flow. Customer is evaluating hosted API for quick experimentation but needs options for Dedicated/VPC for production. Key blockers: data residency, SSO/SAML, predictable latency for inference, and cost per token. Agreed next step: Redwood to share quickstart guide, free credits link, and security overview; schedule SE deep dive and follow-up pilot proposal.
action_items: Sofia to send quickstart link, free credits redemption instructions, and sample cURL by 2026-02-22
Jon to prepare a short perf note on latency for 1k rps and batching tradeoffs by 2026-02-25
Cascade to share expected monthly token volume and compliance checklist by 2026-02-27
next_steps: Share security pack (SOC2, ISO, KMS integration docs)
Set up SE deep dive with infra team (Jon) for dedicated/private sizing
Start a 30-day pilot using hosted API with free credits
transcript: 00:00 Sofia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really quick intro — I'm Sofia from Redwood Inference, AE on this account. Jon is our solutions engineer. 00:08 Priya: Hi, Priya here, Head of ML at Cascade Analytics. We have Ethan and Maya as well. Thanks for doing this. 00:15 Sofia: Great — goal for today is to understand your dev onramp needs, time-to-first-request, and any security constraints. We'll keep it to 40-ish minutes. 00:24 Ethan: Sounds good. High level, we want our data scientists to be able to spin up an experiment in hours, but production needs to be predictable. 00:33 Jon: Awesome — Jon here. Quick question: when you say predictable, are you talking latency SLOs, throughput, or cost predictability? 00:40 Maya: All three I guess. For the initial use case, latency under 250ms p50 for short prompts is preferred, but we're flexible. Cost is a big one — we want to control spend while prototyping. 00:52 Priya: Also need to know timeline for going from playground to prod if it looks good. We have strict data residency requirements for some customers. 01:00 Sofia: Understood. On the PLG side, Redwood's hosted API is meant to be fast to start — free credits, SDKs, cURL examples. Time-to-first-token can be minutes if you use our SDK. 01:12 Priya: Minutes is great, can you walk through an example flow? 01:16 Sofia: Sure — redeem credits, create API key in the console, call POST /v1/generate or use our node client. Jon can show a quick snippet. 01:25 Jon: (brief pause) Right — example: node client .generate with model redwood-alpha, pass prompt, you get streaming tokens. There's also a one-line cURL. We can paste that afterwards. 01:38 Ethan: When you say streaming tokens, is that server-sent events? How's reconnect handled? 01:44 Jon: SSE in hosted mode. On disconnect, the client can rehydrate from the last event-id, and we have KV cache behavior that reduces repeat prefixes — oh that sounded like K V cache — sometimes transcripts flip the name. 01:58 Maya: (laughs) We heard K V cache. 02:02 Priya: For security, we need SSO (SAML/Okta), audit logs, and KMS for encryption. Does Redwood support those out of the box? 02:10 Sofia: Yes — hosted customers can enable SSO via SAML; audit logs and RBAC are in the console tiers. For KMS, dedicated and private options allow customer-managed keys. We have SOC2 Type II reports available. 02:23 Priya: Great. Any limitations on PII or retention? 02:28 Jon: Hosted doesn't store customer prompt/response long-term by default; there's retention controls. For full isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the storage. 02:36 Ethan: If we start on hosted and then move to Dedicated, is the API surface the same? 02:41 Sofia: Exactly the same — same endpoints and SDK, so it's a smooth migration. You can pin model versions and rollout with canary policies. 02:49 Maya: Cost math is important. Can you give us a sense of per-token pricing for hosted and how Dedicated changes that? 02:55 Sofia: Hosted is usage-based; we can send the exact price sheet. Dedicated is reserved capacity — you commit to a baseline and get lower unit costs. Jon will follow up with batching/throughput notes because that affects effective token cost. 03:08 Priya: On the dev onramp, we want to add Redwood to our internal dev portal and give engineers a path to request keys. Is there a self-serve portal API? 03:16 Jon: You can programmatically create API keys via our admin APIs for internal tooling, and we have SDKs. There's also webhook events on usage and quota. 03:24 Maya: Any gotchas for local testing? Do you provide a dockerized runtime? 03:28 Jon: We have an on-prem package for Private, but for quick local dev you can mock responses or use the hosted sandbox. Some customers spin up a small private tenant for integration tests. 03:38 Ethan: About throughput — say we hit 1k requests per second during business hours with batching — what's the recommended approach? 03:45 Jon: For that scale you'd typically look at Dedicated pools with autoscaling and continuous batching. Also prefix caching helps. We'll give a sizing sketch. 03:53 Priya: Can we run a short perf benchmark against our prompts? 03:56 Jon: Absolutely. We can do a 1-2 day benchmark using your prompt set on hosted to baseline latency and token cost, then propose Dedicated sizing. 04:04 Maya: Good. For the pilot, we want to see a gated rollout with canary and fallbacks. Are those supported? 04:10 Sofia: Yes — rollouts and fallback policies are built into Redwood Optimize and the Console. You can set canary percentages and automatic fallback to a cheaper model if latency spikes. 04:21 Ethan: Any limits to the free credits you offer? 04:24 Sofia: The self-serve credits are meant for dev evaluation — typically enough for weeks of testing, but we'll include options for extended pilot credits if needed. 04:33 Priya: About compliance, we need to share an internal checklist — will you provide an official security pack? 04:37 Sofia: Yes, we'll email the pack with SOC2, ISO, encryption details, and the KMS integration guide. 04:44 Maya: Who should we loop in next? 04:46 Priya: I'll add our infra lead and procurement if pricing looks reasonable. 04:50 Sofia: Great. Quick recap: we'll send quickstart + cURL + free credits link, Jon will do the perf note and propose a benchmark, and we'll schedule an SE deep dive for Dedicated sizing. 05:00 Ethan: Sounds good. 05:03 Priya: One more thing — data residency for EU customers. Do you have EU hosted regions? 05:09 Sofia: Yes, we have EU regions and can pin routing for residency; for stricter controls Dedicated or Private works better. 05:18 Maya: For the pilot success criteria: 1) time-to-first-request under 30 minutes for devs, 2) baseline latency under 300ms p50 on our prompts, 3) cost estimate within projection. 05:30 Jon: Noted — we'll design the benchmark to measure p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. 05:36 Sofia: I'll share a short onboarding runbook that shows the steps to go from signup to sample call in under 15 minutes — sometimes docs say minutes but we want a repeatable path. 05:46 Priya: That should help. Anything else on the product side? 05:49 Ethan: A question on model variants — do you host open models and curated variants? 05:53 Jon: Yes, our catalog includes community models and Redwood-verified profiles with recommended quantization and kernel settings. 05:59 Maya: Okay that's helpful. 06:01 Sofia: Final check: we'll send materials by Monday, schedule a 45-minute SE deep dive next week, and set up the pilot. 06:10 Priya: Thanks all. We'll review materials and respond with volumes and compliance checklist. 06:15 Sofia: Perfect, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with links. 06:19 (call ends)
